necmiasfuroglu.name: Hatay Archaeology Museum
necmiasfuroglu.slogan: Roman gods and drinkers underfoot, laid out tile by tile.
necmiasfuroglu.line: The museum shows 3,500 sqm of Antioch's Roman mosaics inside 10,700 sqm of exhibition space.

stpierrecave.name: Cave Church of St Peter
stpierrecave.slogan: A cave where the first Christians are said to have gathered.
stpierrecave.line: Antioch is where, according to Acts 11:26, the disciples were first called Christians; crusaders added the church facade after 1098.

habibineccar.name: Habib-i Neccar Mosque
habibineccar.slogan: Antakya's old mosque, named for a carpenter-saint, rising once more.
habibineccar.line: Among Anatolia's oldest mosques, it fell in the 1853 earthquake and again in February 2023, and is being rebuilt.

titustunnel.name: Titus Tunnel
titustunnel.slogan: Roman legionaries cut a river's new path straight through the rock.
titustunnel.line: Engineers of the Tenth Legion Fretensis cut a canal about 1,400 m long, partly through rock, to divert flood water from the port of Seleucia Pieria.

vakifli.name: Vakıflı
vakifli.slogan: Turkey's last Armenian village, on the slopes of Musa Dagh.
vakifli.line: When Hatay joined Turkey in 1939, Vakıflı's residents chose to stay while six other Armenian villages emigrated to Lebanon.
